recipes.name: Vegan Cupcakes
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup coconut oil, warmed until liquid

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two 12-cup muffin pans or line with 18 paper baking cups.
Pour apple cider vinegar into a 2-cup measuring cup. Fill with almond milk to make 1 1/2 cups. Let stand until curdled, about 5 minutes.

Whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Whisk together almond milk mixture, coconut oil, and vanilla in a separate bowl. Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir just until blended. Spoon batter evenly into the prepared cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until tops spring back when lightly pressed, 15 to 20 minutes. Cool in the pan set over a wire rack.
Arrange cooled cupcakes on a serving platter. Frost with desired frosting.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegan Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: These vegan cupcakes flavored with vanilla are egg-free, made with almond milk and coconut oil, and are quick to make with basic pantry ingredients.

video.description: In this video, we show you how to bake a batch of vegan cupcakes. We use almond milk and coconut oil to keep these treats dairy-free. Try them with rice or coconut milk as well.

review.reviewBody: YUM!!! This recipe is amazing!!! I am an avid baker and love, love, love cupcakes! My tried and true cupcake recipe had previously been a variation of the Magnolia vanilla cupcake recipe, but since my boyfriend's daughter is now a vegan, I needed to find something to bake for her birthday. All I can say is WOW! The texture was great, moist, dense enough (but not too dense), with a faint coconut aroma (due to the coconut oil). My boyfriend actually said these were the best cupcakes I'd ever made and has now been officially converted to a cupcake lover. I served these with a confectioner's sugar "quick frosting": a 1 lb. box of confectioner's sugar, 1/4 c. orange juice (or an orange reduction using vegan butter & agave syrup for a little more flavor), about a 1/2 tbsp. of orange zest, and 1 tsp of bourbon vanilla. I've already made this recipe twice (in two weeks) and will continue to use it, even for my non-vegan friends and family.

I've been looking for a decent vegan vanilla cupcake recipe for quite some time. I think I finally found it. This is by far the best vegan vanilla cupcake I've ever had. The only changes I made to the recipe was to use organic refined coconut oil instead of unrefined because I didn't want a coconut flavor. I also stirred the melted coconut oil into the flour mixture before adding the milk because I've had issues in the past with coconut oil solidifying when added to cold liquid... other than that the recipe was prepared as instructed. Made 17 cupcakes....definitely will make this recipe again and again.

I’m not vegan but I have a friend who is so I wanted to make something sweet I could share with her. These. Are. AMAZING! They’re not too far off in texture from non-vegan cupcakes. They’re moist, not too dense, and perfectly sweet. Just make sure you heat the milk (I used vanilla soy milk, which also adds a little bit to the vanilla flavor!) before you add the warmed coconut oil, as it would likely re-solidify if you were to add it to room-temperature milk. This probably should have been mentioned in the instructions, since not everyone is used to baking with coconut oil. Other than that, the recipe was easy to follow and didn’t take much time to complete at all, and the result tastes sooo good! With some vegan buttercream these will very well be the best cupcakes I’ve ever made!

I used gluten free flour and 1/2 whole milk 1/2 kefir for the milk/vinegar, otherwise followed the directions and they were great!!! The gluten free flour is the Cup4Cup multipurpose gluten free flour.

I added a homemade chai spice powder to the batter which added great flavor. Made it by mixing: 1 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground cloves, 1/2 tsp ground cardamon, 1/2 tsp allspice, 1/2 tsp nutmeg. Also made a vegan buttercream icing with 1 stick of earth balance vegan butter, 2 cps powdered sugar, 1.5 tsp vanilla, 3 tbsp almond milk

This is my first time making vegan cupcakes. I was a bit worried because the recipe note at the top stated that they don’t raise like regular cupcakes. I am an avid baker, and thought maybe it would help the rising process if I sifted the flour and sugar. Oh my they turned out beautiful. They raised perfectly, and tasted scrumptious. I even filled the cupcakes with pie filling apples before baking. I love your recipe, and will for sure use this over and over.

Great recipe! I used lemon instead of vinegar, subbed in about 1/3 of the flour with cocoa powder, used almond extract because I was out of vanilla and added in some chocolate chips. Will definitely make again.

I made these last weekend. I used oat milk instead of soya milk, added one teaspoon of apple sauce to the apple cider vinegar/milk mix and used golden caster sugar as I had no white sugar. Wow, what fantastic cakes! So lovely, moist and delicious. Best cupcakes I've ever made. Will definitely be making them again! Thank you for sharing!

Super easy, fast, and easy to divide or double the recipe. I made it using 1/3 of the ingredients to make 6 cupcakes. Since I’m plant based and celiac, I used Bob’s Red Mill 1:1 all purpose GF flour mix (with the blue labeling-the red has too much garbanzo bean flour and no xanthan gum in the mix), and soy milk. For the “buttercream” I used Earth Balance/vanilla/organic powdered sugar/matcha green tea powder. I’ll definitely be making this recipe again!

This recipe turned out so delicious! I wanted them to be chocolate cupcakes so I only used 1.5 cups of flour and then used .5 cup of cocao powder and they turned out so moist and chocolatey. I also used olive oil in place of the coconut oil.
I made this and added 1 cup finely chopped carrots, 1 teaspoon cinnamon & 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves. Extremely moist & yummy
First vegan cupcakes for the win!
Easy peasy regular freezy. These keep well in the freezer too.

I halved the recipe and changed the milk to whole milk that’s lactose free and it worked great. Love this recipe! Simple and delicious, a new favorite and go to. Thank you for putting realistic cook times for once!!
a yearly birthday request for all 3 kids ! these are a hit in our household. easy, delicious & worth making.
Very bad, too much of oil, my cupcakes became a pancakes. Sad as wasted so much of ingredients
These are so delicious! I followed the recipe as is and they turned out amazing. Thank you!

My friend daughter cannot have eggs or diary. She wanted her birthday to be special with cupcakes. I used this recipe and they went crazy. I have another order for her dance group this time. All the way in sunny Trinidad and Tobago. Thank you🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹🇹
Best cupcakes ever! I liked these way better than nomal cupcakes that use milk and butter.

This cupcake has a very fluffy texture and a punchy batter that I don't usually find in other recipes. I use sunflower oil and golden sugar. Also added fresh juice and zest on 1 big lemon but I didn't feel it neither the vanilla (although my vanilla extract is quite good). That's why I give 4 stars. Next time I'll add more. Otherwise, it's a keep one! Thank you!
